headline: 80 goals scored across 21 World Cup finals in football history
summary: From iconic strikes by legends like Zidane and Messi to a lone own goal, World Cup finals have seen an average of 3.8 goals per match, creating unforgettable moments.
details: A total of 80 goals have been scored across 21 World Cup finals throughout history. The 2026 tournament will be the 23rd edition, but the 1950 format did not include a final match, making the previous 21 finals the basis for this count. On average, 3.8 goals have been scored per final match.

Memorable goals include Di Maria's hard celebration in 2022, Kylian Mbappé's long-range sprint in 2018, and Mario Götze's heart-breaking goal for Argentina in 2014. Andrés Iniesta's iconic goal in 2010, dedicated to his friend Dani Jarque, and Ronaldo Nazário's celebration in 2002 are also etched in history.

From the 1966 final to 2022, 49 goals have been scored in 15 men's World Cup finals, averaging 3.3 goals per match. Only one own goal has ever occurred in a World Cup final, scored by Mario Mandžukić against France in 2018.

Since 1966, only five goals have been scored from outside the penalty box in World Cup finals, according to Opta. Kylian Mbappé's 2018 strike, achieved with 11 touches, is considered the most attractive long-range goal, followed by Brazil's Gerson in 1970. Lionel Messi holds the record for the shortest distance goal in a final, a gentle tap-in in 2022.

Kylian Mbappé holds the record for the most goals in a single World Cup final, scoring four in the 2022 Qatar World Cup. This included a hat-trick during regular play and an additional goal in the penalty shootout.

headline: Saka hattrick seals third place for England in 10-goal thriller
summary: England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 with a thrilling 6-4 victory over France in Miami. Kylian Mbappe also made history, becoming the all-time leading scorer in World Cups.
details: England claimed a dramatic 6-4 victory over France in a high-scoring Miami thriller on Sunday, securing third place for their best World Cup finish since their sole title triumph in 1966. The match saw a total of 10 goals, the highest ever for a third-place playoff, surpassing France's 6-3 win over West Germany in 1958.

Kylian Mbappe scored two goals for France, battling back from a 4-0 deficit. These goals made him the top scorer of the tournament with 10 goals and the all-time leading scorer in World Cups with 22, surpassing Lionel Messi.

Bukayo Saka completed his hattrick from the penalty spot three minutes from time, making it 5-3 and easing England's nerves. He had previously scored twice in the first half, following early goals from Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa that gave England a perfect start.

Despite France's strong second-half comeback, including a strike from Ousmane Dembele, late substitute Jude Bellingham sealed England's victory with his seventh goal of the tournament deep into stoppage time.

The third-place playoff is often considered a match no team wants to play, leading both coaches to make significant team changes. England, perhaps motivated by criticism of their semi-final loss, attacked aggressively from kickoff.

The second half saw a resurgence from France, with Mbappe's double and a goal from Bradley Barcola reducing England's lead to 4-3. However, England maintained their attacking intent when opportunities arose.
This marks England's first third-place finish, having previously lost the playoff matches in 1990 and 2018. Messi will have another chance to increase his tally in the final against Spain.
